data.narrative:
Fairmat, a Series E robotics and manufacturing company that has raised approximately €95M ($103M) to date, is valued against a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company (ticker 277810.KQ) in the robotics and manufacturing sector. The private peer set includes Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics, alongside Generalist AI and Bedrock Robotics.

Peer-Median valuation methodology proved the only applicable triangulation approach. Stage-Progression analysis was excluded after sanity-checking revealed an implied $21.0B valuation—more than 20x total capital raised—indicating an unreliable funding-tracker base value. The Peer-Median method assessed three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: Divergent at Series E valued at $2.3B, Exotec at Series D valued at $2.0B, and Locus Robotics at Series F valued at $2.0B. The median across this set is $2.0B, with a range spanning $2.0B to $2.3B.

Analysis supports a valuation range of $1.7B (low) to $2.3B (high), centered on $2.0B. The limited applicability of only one valuation method and reliance on a three-peer sample represent the primary analytical constraints. Key uncertainties include Fairmat's capital efficiency relative to selected peers, unit economics maturity at Series E, and market-specific growth trajectories within the robotics subsector.
